was: Idaho Power (utility) recreation campground on Brownlee Reservoir, ~23 mi NW of Cambridge on ID-71; 118 RV sites with water + 30-amp electric across four loops (plus 15 walk-in tent sites), showers, dump station, 4-lane boat ramp. Waterfront sites cost $5/night extra. Reservable via CampLife. --Claude
note: Idaho Power park on 65 acres on the Idaho side of Brownlee Reservoir, 23 miles northwest of Cambridge on Idaho Highway 71: four camping loops with 118 RV sites (water and 30-amp power) and 15 walk-in tent sites, showers, a dump station, fire rings, a four-lane boat ramp and docks, a fish-cleaning station and a paved walking path.  Camp hosts are on site from early April to Labor Day.  Utility-run, so ownership is private. --Claude

was: Large lakeside campground on Lost Creek Lake (Rogue River reservoir) between Medford and Crater Lake. Formerly an Oregon State Park; operated by Jackson County Parks since April 1, 2021 (OPRD discounts no longer apply). 151 water/electric sites plus tent sites (200+ total); reservable online (camplife) or by phone. Drive-in, paved loops fit large RVs. --Claude
note: Jackson County park overlooking Lost Creek Lake on the Rogue River, about 40 miles from Crater Lake National Park: 151 sites with water and power (some in B Loop have a lake view), 50 water-only sites in D Loop, flush toilets and hot showers, a dump station, a fenced off-leash dog area, a playground, and hiking trails and bike paths.  The Joseph Stewart Resort in the day-use area has a camp store, a small café and a marina that rents boats and moorage, typically from mid-April through October.  Oregon State Parks discounts and waivers haven't applied since Jackson County Parks took over on April 1, 2021. --Claude

season.note: Only one loop stays open in winter.

was: Linn County park on Green Peter Reservoir near Foster; 85 sites (incl 4 pull-throughs) in 3 forested loops, no hookups, plus yurts; vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat ramp. Open ~mid-Apr to late-Sep, reservable. --Claude
note: Primitive Linn County park on 328 forested acres on Green Peter Reservoir near Sweet Home, 12 miles from the intersection of Hwy. 20 and Quartzville Road: sites without hookups (four are double pull-throughs for 2 RVs), yurts, vault restrooms and hand-pump water.
